title: Create GameState
unlocks: A real build system, and code you can navigate.
objective: Restructure the exact same game into classes across multiple files, and build it with CMake instead of typing g++ by hand. The behaviour must not change at all -- that is the whole test.

git: a real merge conflict, in a file you wrote

checks: my-game/CMakeLists.txt exists and the project builds with no warnings.
The CMake targets `my_game` (a library) and `ttt-cli` (an executable) both exist.
Every Stage 2 behaviour check still passes against the new binary.
Your game logic lives somewhere other than main.cpp.
hints: You have a board, and you have things you do to a board. In C++ those can live together in one type. What state does your game need to remember between moves? That list is your class's member variables.
Two different jobs again: one type that HOLDS the game (board, whose turn, whether it is over), and code that CHANGES it. They can be one class or two -- decide which, and be able to say why.

class Board:
    data: nine cells
    method: what is at cell i
    method: put a mark at cell i
    method: is cell i empty

main.cpp: create one, loop, call its methods

When you add a second .cpp file you must add it to `add_library(my_game ...)` in my-game/CMakeLists.txt. If you forget, the code compiles fine and then the LINKER fails with 'undefined reference to ...'. That distinction -- compiled but not linked -- is the single most useful build concept in C++, and you are about to meet it for real.

prompts.title: undefined reference / linker error
prompts.body:
I am getting an error building my C++ project with CMake.

Here is the full output:
<PASTE THE ERROR>

Here is my my-game/CMakeLists.txt:
<PASTE IT>

First tell me whether this is a COMPILER error or a LINKER error, and how I can tell the difference from the message alone. Then ask me which files I have created. Do not fix it for me.

prompts.title: Review my class design
prompts.body:
I have just turned my tic-tac-toe program into classes.

Here are my files:
<PASTE THEM>

Ask me questions about the design. Specifically: what is the responsibility of each class in one sentence, which member functions should be const and why, and is there anything public that should not be? Do not redesign it for me -- if you think something is wrong, ask me a question that helps me see it.

prompts.title: Quiz me on classes and const
prompts.body:
Quiz me on C++ classes: struct vs class, constructors, member functions, and const member functions.

One question at a time. Include at least one question about what `const` after a member function actually promises, and one about what happens if I forget to initialise a member. Wait for my answer before moving on.
